question: In 2 Samuel 7 (the Davidic Covenant), what does God promise David, and how does the NT interpret its fulfillment?

choices.A: God promises David an eternal dynasty and a son who will build God's house and whose kingdom will endure forever — the NT sees this fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David, whose kingdom is the Church and whose reign is eternal
choices.B: God promises David personal wealth and military victory over all his enemies in his lifetime
choices.C: God promises to preserve Jerusalem forever from any foreign conquest
choices.D: God promises David that his son Solomon will be the final and greatest king with no successor needed

teaching.title: The Davidic Covenant — 2 Samuel 7
teaching.body: In 2 Samuel 7:12-16, God tells David through Nathan: 'I will raise up your offspring after you... I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever... I will be his father and he will be my son... your house and your kingdom shall endure forever before me.' Solomon partially fulfilled this — he built the Temple. But no Davidic king maintained an eternal throne; the line was broken in the Babylonian exile. The NT presents Jesus as the definitive fulfillment: the angel tells Mary he will be given 'the throne of his father David and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever' (Luke 1:32-33). The genealogies (Matt 1, Luke 3) trace his Davidic descent. The resurrection inaugurates the eternal reign promised.
